channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Choosing a Machine Learning Engineer Career Path
item.description: Research, platform, and applied ML are different jobs wearing the same title. Here is how to tell them apart before you commit years to one.

item.title: Deep Learning with Python Style Books: What They Teach, What They Skip
item.description: Python deep learning books build strong intuition fast, but leave evaluation rigour, leakage, and deployment realities largely untouched.

item.title: What a Deep Learning Definition Should Really Include
item.description: Glossary definitions of deep learning describe architecture, not behaviour. Here is what they usually leave out, and why it matters.

item.title: Machine Learning Play: Why Toy Demos Rarely Mirror Production
item.description: Toy ML demos look like competence but hide the hard parts: leakage-free splits, drift, latency, and monitoring. Here is why that gap matters.

item.title: Data Science vs Data Analytics Adverts: Reading Between the Lines
item.description: Same title, wildly different jobs. Learn to read adverts for the actual work: modelling versus reporting, ambiguity versus dashboards.

item.title: A Beginner's Roadmap into Machine Learning, and Why Order Matters
item.description: A practical order for learning machine learning, from maths to baselines to evaluation, and why skipping steps costs you later.

item.title: Deep Learning Super Sampling: Borrowed Ideas, False Friends
item.description: DLSS borrows the machinery of supervised super-resolution but has nothing to do with language models or generative chat. Here is the actual lineage.

item.title: Prompt Engineering From First Principles: What It Covers
item.description: A grounded look at what prompt engineering really means: specification, context control, and systematic evaluation, not just clever wording tricks.

item.title: A Plain Guide to Fine-Tuning LLMs
item.description: Fine-tuning rarely rewrites a model's knowledge. It mostly reweights how existing knowledge gets expressed. Here is the honest version of what changes.

item.title: Data Science Certifications Versus What Employers Actually Screen For
item.description: Certifications prove you finished a syllabus. Hiring screens test whether you can reason under uncertainty, debug, and communicate. The overlap is smaller than people assume.

item.title: LLM Arenas Versus Fixed Benchmarks: Which Evaluation Wins
item.description: Arenas measure what people prefer; benchmarks measure what models can do. Confusing the two produces confident, misleading leaderboards.

item.title: Reading an LLM Leaderboard Without Mistaking Rank for Capability
item.description: A top rank on an LLM leaderboard tells you less than you think. Here is how to interrogate the numbers before trusting them.

item.title: What a Model Evaluation Framework Hides in Its Defaults
item.description: Default settings in evaluation frameworks are design choices, not neutral facts. Knowing what they hide saves you from publishing misleading numbers.

item.title: Picking a Model Evaluation Technique for Your Actual Problem
item.description: K-fold is not a default you apply everywhere. Match the evaluation scheme to how your data was generated and how the model will actually be used.

item.title: Computer Vision Syndrome vs Computer Vision: A Naming Clash
item.description: Computer vision syndrome is an eye strain condition; computer vision is a branch of AI. The shared name causes real confusion in search, citations, and casual conversation.

item.title: Data Science Major vs Minor: What Each Prepares You For
item.description: A data science major builds you to design and evaluate methods; a minor builds you to apply them responsibly. Knowing which one you are getting changes how you plan your career.

item.title: How Many Fine-Tuning Examples Do You Actually Need
item.description: Fine-tuning does not need thousands of examples to work. It needs the right examples, tested the right way.

item.title: Fine-Tuning Synonyms: Why Precise Language Matters
item.description: Calling everything 'fine-tuning' hides what you actually did. Precise method language is a reproducibility issue, not pedantry.

item.title: Why LLM Wikis and Glossaries Disagree on Basic Terms
item.description: Why does every LLM glossary define 'hallucination' or 'grounding' differently? A practical guide to choosing and defending your own working definitions.

item.title: Data Science Versus Data Analytics: Why It Matters
item.description: Same buzzwords, different jobs. Here is the concrete distinction between data science and data analytics, and why conflating them causes bad hires and worse projects.
